key_insight: Not all Transformer layers should be adapted equally: choosing low-similarity layers for fine-tuning can improve task performance while preserving more of the model’s general abilities.
engineering_relevance: Layer-selective adaptation offers a simple, compute-aware PEFT strategy for deploying LLMs on math and code tasks without as much capability drift.
method: Measure layer sensitivity with empirical Fisher information.
Use input–output cosine similarity as a forward-only proxy to rank layers.
Apply LoRA only to layers with low input–output similarity (LS-LoRA).
evidence_signal: Across mathematical reasoning and code generation benchmarks, LS-LoRA improved average target-task performance and retained substantially more commonsense reasoning capability than standard all-layer LoRA.
watch_item: The layer-ranking proxy may depend on model and task settings, so the selected layers should be validated before deployment.
paper_title: Where to Adapt Matters: Layer-Selective Fine-Tuning for Capability Retention
